knowledge:
- key_parameters: x=pedigree data frame or Pedigree object ;; subject=column name for individual ID ;; ascendant=vector of column names for parents/ascendants ;; ascendantSex=vector of sexes corresponding to ascendants ;; sex=column name for individual sex ;; object=Pedigree object in model.matrix ;; y=phenotype vector ;; id=individual ID vector in model.matrix
- alternatives: PEDIG (Fortran package for pedigree analysis in large populations) ;; Meuwissen and Luo (1992) algorithm for inbreeding coefficients ;; Sargolzaei et al. (2005) fast algorithm for inbreeding coefficients
- when_to_use: When performing quantitative genetics analyses, specifically setting up mixed model equations (animal models) and calculating additive genetic relationship matrices or their inverses from pedigree data.
- pitfalls: Ensure the pedigree is extended using extend() before calculating the inverse additive relationship matrix (inverseAdditive) to include all founders and ancestors without records in the matrix.

workflows.name: quantitative_genetics_animal_model
workflows.intent: Set up and solve mixed model equations for an animal model using pedigree data and phenotypes.
input: pedigree_data.csv (data frame containing individual, sire, dam, sex, and phenotype columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Create a Pedigree object ;; 2. Generate the design matrix for random animal effects ;; 3. Extend the pedigree to include all ancestors ;; 4. Compute the inverse of the additive genetic relationship matrix ;; 5. Set up the coefficient matrix (LHS) and right-hand side (RHS) equations ;; 6. Solve the mixed model equations for breeding values and fixed effects
workflows.code:
library(GeneticsPed)
data(Mrode3.1)
(x <- Pedigree(x=Mrode3.1, subject="calf", ascendant=c("sire", "dam"),
               ascendantSex=c("Male", "Female"), sex="sex"))
(y <- x$pwg)
X <- model.matrix(~ x$sex - 1)
t(X)
(Z <- model.matrix(object=x, y=x$pwg, id=x$calf))
(LHS <- rbind(cbind(crossprod(X),    crossprod(X, Z)),
              cbind(crossprod(Z, X), crossprod(Z))))
x <- extend(x)
Ainv <- inverseAdditive(x=x)
sigma2a <- 20
sigma2e <- 40
alpha <- sigma2e / sigma2a
q <- nIndividual(x)
p <- nrow(LHS) - q
(LHS[(p + 1):(p + q), (p + 1):(p + q)] <-
 LHS[(p + 1):(p + q), (p + 1):(p + q)] + Ainv * alpha)
RHS <- rbind(crossprod(X, y),
             crossprod(Z, y))
sol <- solve(LHS, RHS)
t(sol)
